frequency_question: What proportion of transferred complex missile technologies successfully establish verified domestic operational production lines within a tight two-to-three-year window?
membership_rule: Includes: licensed domestic production or major assembly initiatives for complex guided weapons transferred to a recipient nation. Excludes: simple maintenance, basic ordnance refitting, non-missile conventional arms, or peacetime standard tech transfers.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production of Stugna-P/Neptune components
Taiwan Hsiung Feng missile domestic scaling
South Korea licensed production of advanced tactical missiles
Attempted rapid transfer and domestic assembly of complex Western air defense systems in emergency zones without prior industrial baselines

provenance_note: 4 cases named, 5 claimed via skeleton x multiplier (1.2x)
coverage_note: 4 named instances in the primary dataset; estimated 5 total relevant modern high-tech missile localization attempts under urgent conditions.
known_gaps: Classified nature of deep bilateral defense industrial transfers limits complete enumeration of failed secret attempts.
skeleton: Total verified tech-transfer attempts for high-end missiles divided by those achieving operational domestic assembly confirmed by public defense press within the window.
validity_reason: Defense industrial base transfer timelines and geopolitical secrecy norms remain stable over the medium term.
